title: Simplest: faith justifies because it is imputed to the believer for righteousness
source_text: XXII. Simplicissimum nobis videtur si dicamus, fidem justificare, quia credenti, sua fides imputatur ad justitiam. Sic enim Apostolus ipse mentem suam explicat, de justificatione per fidem ex professo agens, Rom. 4. Credenti, inquit, in eum qui justificat impium, reputatur fides ejus ad justitiam. Et in hunc finem citat illud Mosis, Credidit Abraham Deo, & reputatum est ei ad justitiam. Fides autem ad justitiam imputari dicitur, quia Deus illum qui viva fide in Christum credit pro justo habet & reputat, eum a poena peccati liberans, & ad vitam aeternam acceptans, propter Christi mortem & obedientiam.
pass_a_gloss: It seems simplest to us if we say that faith justifies because to the believer his faith is imputed for righteousness. For so the Apostle himself explains his mind when treating justification by faith expressly in Romans 4. To the one who believes, he says, in him who justifies the ungodly, his faith is counted for righteousness. And to this end he cites Moses' word: Abraham believed God, and it was counted to him for righteousness. But faith is said to be imputed for righteousness because God holds and counts as just the one who believes in Christ with living faith, freeing him from sin's punishment and accepting him to eternal life because of Christ's death and obedience.
pass_b_english: Simplest: faith justifies because it is imputed to the believer for righteousness (Rom 4).
God counts the living believer just for Christ's death and obedience.

choices.why: Paul's Rom 4 account of justifying faith.
